title: JavaScript Errors in TypeScript knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a reliable TypeScript integration do with external data?
options: Assume the declared type validates the server response.
Ignore promise rejections and malformed data.
Treat JSON.parse as a validation step.
Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
questions.answer_key: Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
questions.explanation: Types and runtime validation solve different problems at external boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “JavaScript Errors in TypeScript”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with error objects and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with error objects and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Error objects”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “JavaScript Errors in TypeScript”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check try...catch, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume the type of caught values is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check try...catch, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “try...catch”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
